idiom_name: Django MIDDLEWARE factories (get_response) / WSGI-ASGI middleware callables
implementation_notes: Python's dominant frameworks define the contract: Django loads the MIDDLEWARE list of factories, each taking get_response and returning a callable that receives the request - the Context - and may short-circuit by returning a response without calling get_response (middleware runs top-down on the way in and reversed on the way out, the onion model). ASGI/WSGI middleware is the same shape at a lower level: a callable wrapping the next application, async def app(scope, receive, send). The classic Interceptor/Dispatcher classes are replaced by callables plus the framework's middleware list; decorators (functools.wraps) are the local idiom when the concern belongs to one function rather than to a framework event, and a hand-written registry remains the norm for framework-agnostic library code.
code_sketch:
class TimingMiddleware:
    def __init__(self, get_response):         # constructed once at startup
        self.get_response = get_response

    def __call__(self, request):              # invoked per request
        t0 = time.perf_counter()
        try:
            return self.get_response(request)  # downstream chain
        finally:
            metrics.observe(request.path, time.perf_counter() - t0)
pitfalls: Middleware is instantiated once per process and reused across threads/tasks, so request state must never be stored on self - use the request object or contextvars.

Skipping get_response silently short-circuits the view and every inner middleware, and the response then never passes the outer response-phase hooks (process_exception/process_template_response) - a debugging middleware that swallows requests is hard to spot.
Sync/async mismatch: a middleware must declare what it supports (async_capable) or the server picks the wrong wrapper, and a blocking call inside async middleware blocks the whole event loop.
Exception-phase methods run in reverse order and only for middlewares the request actually reached; ordering mistakes turn exception handling into unexplained 500s.
